question.problem:
The inverse of the $2\times 2$ matrix $P$ is found using row operations, as shown below. Complete the process, and determine ${P}^{-1}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}[P\,|\,I] & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=-\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{1}{3} & -\frac{1}{3} & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{1}{3} & -\frac{1}{3} & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{5}{3} & \frac{2}{3} & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{3}{5}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{1}{3} & -\frac{1}{3} & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{2}{5} & \frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & \bbox[2pt,lightgray]{\phantom{a}} & \bbox[2pt,lightgray]{\phantom{a}} \\ 0 & 1 & \bbox[2pt,lightgray]{\phantom{a}} & \bbox[2pt,lightgray]{\phantom{a}}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
We write down $P$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $P$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[P\,|\,I] & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=-\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{1}{3} & -\frac{1}{3} & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{1}{3} & -\frac{1}{3} & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{5}{3} & \frac{2}{3} & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{3}{5}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{1}{3} & -\frac{1}{3} & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{2}{5} & \frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -\frac{1}{5} & \frac{1}{5} \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{2}{5} & \frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The matrix ${P}^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, 

$$
{P}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{5} & \frac{1}{5} \\ \frac{2}{5} & \frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}].
$$
